content_of_post_to_comment:
I am a first time homeowner and have been terrible at doing basic home maintenance and upkeep for my house. I’m not very knowledgeable or handy, so i feel like that adds to me putting things off. Some examples are:

* I frequently put off changing any filters (hvac, water filters, etc)
* I never inspect major appliances and areas seasonally which was a MAJOR problem recently because my water heater had been leaking bad for a while and caused mold.
* i do the bare minimum with landscaping and yard upkeep (just mow the lawn never pull weeds)

And on top of the bad routine maintenance, i don’t even have improvements on my radar. It’s like nothing registers to me until it’s an emergency. I see most neighbors gardening or installing some sort of upgraded fixtures outside their homes and I feel like a lazy POS.

Tl;DR: how do I get myself to actually take care of my home?
comment: The water heater situation is a good example of why home maintenance feels overwhelming: most tasks are invisible until they become disasters. I started treating my house like a car with a basic service schedule instead of waiting until something broke. A simple monthly reminder list for filters, leaks, gutters, etc. made it much less mentally exhausting.
